_source.title: NASA/Keck Reflectance Experiment Laboratory
description: Updated schema version. Adding missing "investigation" references.

The Keck/NASA Reflectance Experiment Laboratory (RELAB) is a multi-user spectroscopy facility supported by NASA. RELAB has two operational spectrometers available to NASA scientists: 1) a near-ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared bidirectional spectrometer and 2) a near- and mid- infrared FT-IR spectrometer. The overall purpose of the design and operation of the RELAB bidirectional spectrometer is to obtain high precision, high spectral resolution, bidirectional reflectance spectra of earth and planetary materials. Spectroscopic data acquired in the laboratory provide the interpretive foundation upon which compositional information about unexplored or unsampled planetary surfaces is derived from remotely obtained reflectance spectra. One of the key elements of the design of RELAB is the ability to measure samples using viewing geometries specified by the user. This allows investigators to simulate the geometry of natural observing conditions for particulate samples as small as 50 mg. Laboratory time can be made available at no charge to investigators who are in funded NASA programs. For more information, see https://sites.brown.edu/relab/.
